questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have been to Barcelona a couple of times before and I really love the city. The fact that it is a big international city but also surrounded by nature and the sea was definitely important to me. Furthermore I really wanted to go to a Spanish speaking country to refresh my Spanish, and even though they mostly speak Catalan in Barcelona, I have definitely improved my Spanish.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The experience as a whole has been absolutely amazing!!! The administrative things around the university was a little slow, but everything worked out fine, so it was not a major thing.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I managed to find everything I needed, but you have to keep up yourself and make sure that you have everything under control about the necessary documents and everything. But if you do that, it was definitely manageable.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of intro sessions in the beginning that you could sign up for. It was a bit chaotic and with a lot of people, but some of it was useful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found mine through a Facebook group and I git extremely lucky and had the best experience in my flat!! There is a lot of scam in Barcelona, so you should be careful paying anything, before you are sure that it is actually real! If you don't have the option to go see it, make a video call, do it through an agency (even though you will probably have to pay an agency fee) and if the flat has multiple rooms, try to get in touch with several people, so that you're sure that it's legit. Also in February (and August/September I think) there are a lot of students looking for housing, so you should start looking early and continuously!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend living off campus, in the city of Barcelona. Barcelona is amazing and I know a lot of people who moved off campus because it was annoying when they had to go into the city or back from the city (especially at night, because then you have to take a bus or taxi). In my experience, you're missing out on quite a lot, if you live on campus, and a lot of other international students live in the city!!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It can be hard to find something as many are looking, and it is quite expensive. But I ended up in a great student flat and I know many people who did too, so there are many opportunities :-)

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After I received my pre approval I had to fill out a form for the host university, but everything is done by email, so it took a while, as I had to wait for them to reply. It was also a bit hard to figure out the language of the courses (but apparently if it says partly English, partly Spanish, it will be in Spanish - and the same with Catalan). I also had to get a signature at the administration office, which is not open that many hours a week, which was a bit annoying.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: If you seem desperate enough in your emails, they are okay at replying (somewhat quickly), and helping you figuring everything out.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: One of the classes I wanted was unfortunately cancelled that semester, but beside that, I got the classes I wanted in the first place. However, when I found out that one course was fully in Spanish, they told me that the class I wanted to change to was full (even though it didn't seem like it from what I heard from other students in the class). If I had been more persistent, I might have been able to switch, but that was a bit annoying (but I guess fair, as the class had already started).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware about the language of the class! And be persistent with your emails to them - if you seem desperate enough, they will answer!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In general it seems like the expected level at the exams and assignments has been a bit lower, but during the classes the level was okay. Some of my classes here, were partly similar to classes I already had at UCPH, but the level was still okay.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of the classes were pretty similar (the teacher presented the content of the class and then we participated in some discussions). The classes were a bit smaller, which was nice. They did more continuous assessment than I'm used to from UCPH (weekly quizzes, assignments, presentations), which was actually quite nice, as your whole grade doesn't come down to one exam. However the amount of assignments I had to write, was a bot overwhelming (but maybe mostly because I did them last minute...).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Socio-Political Marketing (10 ECTS)
European Integration (10 ECTS)
Polítiques Migratòries i Integració Social / Migration and Integration Policies (10 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Socio-Political Marketing class was really interesting and it was divided in five parts, so we had a lot of different professors which was cool. That also meant that we got to work in different ways, which was also nice.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I spilled coffee in my computer, which was a bit unexpected and expensive to fix, but otherwise nothing really :-)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: A little bit more expensive to do grocery shopping than I expected, but on the other hand it's quite cheap to go out for dinner and drinks/coffee.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: As I lived in the city center and UAB was 50 minutes away, I didn't really look for activities at the uni, so I actually don't know.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It was not really connected to the host university, but ESN do a lot of activities and the app Erasmus Barcelona is also good to have (they also do trips and stuff).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Montserrat, all the museums in Barcelona, some of the beaches outside of Barcelona (Castelldefels, Sitges, Vilanova, etc.), go on some hiking trips in the areas around Barcelona. I know a lot of students went on weekend trips to Valencia, Mallorca, Menorca, etc. which is supposed to be really nice (and cheap).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was surprisingly easy to fall into the Spanish chill vibe (which I don't think is necessarily a good thing), but the Catalan people are in general hard to get close with (they're quite closed and mostly keeps to themselves).

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: To be honest I didn't really socialize that much with local students myself - all of my courses were mostly with other exchange students, and I lived with other exchange students, so it was difficult to get in touch with the locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I think mostly that fact that everything works slower here than in Denmark, but otherwise I easily felt like Barcelona was my home.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food is really nice and the architecture of the city!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Be persistent with your emails when you have to figure out the enrollment and the registration in courses - sound desperate if necessary; 2) If possible, do your work during the semester, so you can enjoy your last time here (especially if it's summer; 3) Don't freak out if everything seems a bit unorganized - it's gonna fall into place!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is a bit outside the city, but the train ride there is really nice :)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting amazing people from all over the world and really being on my own and out of my comfort zone! I have learned so much and I've had some of the best experiences here!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Fighting a bit with my landlord about stuff in the apartment and maybe figuring everything out at the university (but these have been minor things and it hasn't really bothered me that much)

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Barcelona is truly an amazing city to be an exchange student in!!! So many international students, many different areas in the city, the beach, the nature around Barcelona and the restaurants and bars :-D

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
